title: How to Prepare for a Root Canal Appointment
metaTitle: Preparing for a Root Canal Appointment: A Checklist
metaDescription: A calm, practical guide to preparing for a root canal: what to eat, which medications to mention, questions to ask, and how to plan your day around the visit.
excerpt: A little preparation makes a root canal go more smoothly. Here is a practical checklist, from meals and medications to questions worth asking and planning your day.
heroImageAlt: A person writing a short list of questions before a dental appointment.
bodyHtml:
How to prepare for a root canal

Preparing for a root canal is mostly about a few simple, practical steps: eat a normal meal beforehand unless your dentist tells you otherwise, take your usual medications as directed, bring a list of questions, and plan a calm, unhurried day around the appointment. There is no complicated preparation for a standard root canal done with local anaesthetic — and knowing that in advance can itself take some of the worry out of it. The points below walk through what actually helps.

In the days before

  • Confirm the details. Note the date, time, and location, and give yourself extra travel time so you are not rushing.
  • Write down your questions. It is easy to forget them in the chair. Jot down anything you want to understand — how many visits, what you will feel, what the aftercare is, when you will get the permanent restoration.
  • Review your medications and health history. Make a list of everything you take, including over-the-counter items and supplements, and note any allergies. Tell your dentist about conditions such as heart problems or anything that affects bleeding or healing. Do not stop any prescribed medication without checking with the professional who prescribed it.
  • Flag anything new. If you have been unwell, started a new medication, or have swelling or a fever, let the clinic know in advance.

On the day

  • Eat beforehand. Unlike surgery with general anaesthetic, a standard root canal with local anaesthetic does not usually require an empty stomach. Because your mouth will be numb for a few hours afterward, having a meal before the appointment is often the more comfortable choice. (If any form of sedation is planned, your clinic will give you specific instructions, which may differ — always follow those.)
  • Brush as usual. Arriving with a clean mouth is appreciated and perfectly fine.
  • Dress comfortably. You may be in the chair for a while, so wear something relaxed and consider bringing headphones if music helps you stay calm.
  • Go easy on caffeine. If coffee tends to make you jittery, you might keep it light so you feel steadier.

Planning the rest of your day

Most people feel well enough to return to normal activities after a root canal done with local anaesthetic, but it is sensible not to pack your schedule too tightly. Your lip, cheek, or tongue may stay numb for a few hours, so plan to avoid eating until feeling returns, and expect some mild tenderness around the tooth for a few days. Having some soft foods at home and your preferred over-the-counter pain relief on hand means you are not scrambling later. If you have young children or caregiving duties, it can help to arrange a little support for the afternoon so you are not under pressure to rush straight back into a busy routine before the freezing has worn off.

Should I take painkillers before I arrive?

Do not take anything specifically for the appointment without checking with your dentist first, since recommendations depend on your health and what is planned. It is always fine, and helpful, to ask the clinic in advance what they suggest for before and after.

Can I drive myself home?

With local anaesthetic only, most people can drive themselves, as numbness is not the same as impairment. If any sedation is involved, you will likely need to arrange a ride. Clarify this with your clinic when you book so there are no surprises.

What should I bring?

Bring your list of questions, your medication and allergy information, your insurance or dental plan details if relevant, and anything that helps you relax, such as headphones. If you are anxious, it can help to bring a supportive friend or family member.

A calm, prepared start

Walking in feeling organised and informed makes the whole experience easier. If you would like to go over any of this before your visit or book an appointment, you can reach the team at Smile Dental Arts Centre in Markham, or request a time through the clinic's appointments page. Dr. Neda Kadivar is a general and family dentist with over 20 years of experience.
